description: You come off the Exchange floor with a few Crowns for a sack of Rat Scrap, and find Inspector Rook at the counter you have just left, reading the clerk's ledger upside down. She closes it, turns, and asks whether you enjoyed the view from the bottom rim lately. The Gaugers, she adds, take an interest in private readings of the Scald. Her notebook is already open and her pencil already sharpened, as if the answer were written somewhere and only wanted copying out.

options.label: Tell her the truth: you took a reading, and it disagreed with the Gazette by 40 fathoms.

success.text: Rook writes it down without comment, then reads it back to you, and it sounds worse in her voice. She asks to borrow Mother Ash's pocket gauge, as evidence. It will be returned, she says, in due course, which at Gaugehill is a unit of time. You hand it over. Somebody in the Lowvents will hear about that by supper.

options.label: Tell her you were mending a vent for Mother Ash, and nothing more.

success.text: "A vent," says Rook. "Of course." She writes that down too, in the same neat hand, and underlines nothing. Then she thanks you for your time, touches her hat, and walks away in the direction of somewhere you were planning to go next.

options.label: Excuse yourself into the crowd on the trading floor and leave by the coal door.

success.text: The trading floor swallows you gladly, and the coal door lets you out into an alley at the cost of one shin, barked hard on the chute. You limp home the long way round. Rook does not follow. She does not, you suspect, need to.
